title: Dropout voltage at 50mA load (Vin sweep toward Vout, DR-003/gf180 convention)
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Dropout @ 50 mA" row (< 300mV, stretch goal < 200mV) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch), using the ratified row's own cited method ("gf180's ss/125C/Vin~=Vout+dropout convention"): fix I_LOAD at 50mA (the row's own test point) and sweep Vin down toward Vout to find the Vin-Vout margin at which regulation is lost, rather than sweeping load current at a single ample Vin (that measures load regulation, a different spec row). That row is ratified by issue #1 / DR-006, and the bound below cites it verbatim, not an invented final limit. Methodology fixed by issue #71 (superseding #18's original method): the deck sweeps VIN downward, from a comfortably-regulating value toward a value well below the 1.8V target, at a finer (20mV) resolution than #18's original 50mV; dropout_v is the Vin-Vout margin at the VIN where VOUT first falls (`.meas dc ... fall=1`) through 98% of the 1.8V target as VIN decreases -- the classic "regulation just lost" dropout definition -- not a fixed low-VIN endpoint (#18's method reported the pass device's residual V_sd well past dropout, overstating the gap; see #71's PR for the derivation and design/README.md's campaign section for the closed-loop screening that motivated the fix). vout_at_max_vin_v is a light-headroom regulation sanity check at the sweep's top (first-swept) end. INITIAL-CONDITION CONTRACT (#171, converted by #178): the analysis is no longer a `dc VVIN 3.63 1.5 -0.02` sweep. It is ONE cold-start, settled transient ('tran 10u 14m uic') in which VIN is a PWL ramp -- 0V to the corner's own 'vsup' top by 100us, EN stepping high at 100us to that same 'vsup' (issue #187), the ideal 50mA sink ramped on over 2.5-2.6ms once the loop is up (sim/ic-screen-125c-c's own cold-start convention, verbatim), settled by 5.5ms, then VIN walked DOWN from 'vsup' to 'vsup'-2.13V over 6ms-14ms -- a CONSTANT 266.3 V/s at every corner, the endpoint tracking 'vsup' precisely so the rate does not -- as a quasi-static line droop -- so there is no operating-point solve in the deck at all: the contract's 'uic' + EN-edge shape, the one PR #170 landed for mc-output-accuracy and #172 for line-/load-regulation. WHY a shape change rather than a seed: ngspice honours neither accepted seed shape for a `dc` analysis. Measured during #178 on this bench (tt/125C/3.30V, the eleven-node `.ic` card copied verbatim from sim/ic-screen-125c-b): the seeded `dc` sweep flails exactly as the unseeded one does -- 'singular matrix' x6, 'Dynamic gmin stepping failed' x16, 'out of range for ^' x13, with iterates at 1e155-1e188 V on the sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po body expressions -- because `.ic` is applied to the operating-point solve preceding a non-'uic' transient, not to a `dc` sweep's solves; and #172 measured the other half, that `.nodeset` (which a bare solve does honour) still printed 'singular matrix' plus 'Dynamic gmin stepping failed' at 3 of 5 corners probed. A seed could in any case only fix the sweep's FIRST point, and the superseded record 20260923-123440-d71f4b3 carries thousands of diagnostics per corner log (45 of 45 corners diagnosed), i.e. the continuation loses the branch repeatedly all the way down the sweep -- which sim/bin/corner-run.py's #171 gate now forces to FAIL outright. QUASI-STATIC, MEASURED not assumed -- a three-point ramp-rate series at tt/27C/3.30V, all three with zero solver diagnostics: 8ms ramp (266.3 V/s) reads dropout_v = 0.397657V, 20ms ramp (106.5 V/s) reads 0.397295V, 60ms ramp (35.5 V/s) reads 0.398492V. The spread over a 7.5x rate range is 1.2mV with no monotone trend -- the answer is rate-INDEPENDENT in this window, not merely 'slow enough' -- and the superseded `dc` record, the zero-rate limit of the same experiment, reads 0.399743V at that corner, 2.1mV above the 8ms ramp (the `dc` sweep's own 20mV grid interpolation). The whole 2.4mV span sits against a 300mV ratified bound; the matrix runs the 8ms ramp because it is inside the rate-independent window and costs 22s per corner where the 60ms ramp cost 471s. SUPPLY AXIS, corrected by issue #187: 'vsup' now sets the DUT's actual VIN -- the ramp starts at 'vsup' and EN's high level is that same 'vsup' -- rather than EN's rail alone. Through record 20260926-043132-eba96ae (#178) VIN was pinned at 3.63V for every corner, inherited unchanged from the `dc` sweep's own first point, while 'vsup' drove EN only; that put EN 0.66V BELOW VIN at the '*_2.97v' corners, which is off the DUT's documented enable interface (design/README.md "Enable/shutdown": EN is active-high, full-rail 0V/VIN) and is what stopped the block coming up at fs_125c_2.97v (vout_at_max_vin_v = -7.4521V there, with no solver diagnostic). #187 measured the mechanism -- the M_ENP/M_ENP2 shutdown clamps conduct 1.377uA/1.639uA at EN = VIN-0.66V against 39pA/62pA at EN = VIN, while the amplifier's own tail current falls from 3.476uA to 1.003uA because M_ENP2's injection lifts BIASP 90.6mV -- and replaced the convention with the one every other bench in sim/ already uses (VIN = 'vsup', EN = 'vsup'). dropout_v is unaffected: holding the down-ramp RATE constant (the endpoint tracks 'vsup' at 'vsup'-2.13V rather than being pinned at 1.5V) reproduces the superseded record's crossing exactly -- fs_125c_2.97v's crossing VIN reads 2.19615V under both conventions, i.e. dropout_v = 0.432153V to six digits -- so the correction moves vout_at_max_vin_v and nothing else. WHY THE RATE IS HELD CONSTANT, measured: the first #187 re-run (record 20260926-100003-0b63ae4, superseded by this one) kept the fixed 1.5V endpoint, which makes the rate per-supply (183.8/225.0/266.3 V/s) and moved dropout_v by up to 20.4mV across the supply axis at the cold/slow corners (ss/27C 0.379823V at 2.97V vs 0.400265V at 3.63V; tt/-40C 0.452920V vs 0.472185V; sf/-40C 0.535094V vs 0.554380V), monotone with rate and in the direction #178's own ramp-rate caveat documents. That is real rate-dependence at those corners rather than noise, so the bench keeps the supply axis a pure supply axis instead of confounding supply with ramp rate.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * ONE cold-start transient, not a `dc VVIN` sweep (issue #178, the #171
* initial-condition contract): `uic` starts every node at its natural cold
* value with EN low, the testbench's VEN steps high at 100us, VIN rises to
* the corner's own 'vsup' top by 100us, the ideal 50mA sink ramps on over
* 2.5-2.6ms once the loop is up, and the block is settled by 5.5ms. VIN is
* then ramped DOWN from 'vsup' to 'vsup'-2.13V over 6ms-14ms -- a CONSTANT
* 266.3 V/s at every corner, quasi-static (see the testbench header for the
* ramp-rate measurement and for why the endpoint tracks 'vsup' instead of
* being pinned at 1.5V) -- and the dropout crossing is read off that ramp.
* SUPPLY CONVENTION (issue #187): VIN's top is 'vsup' and EN's high level
* is that same 'vsup', so EN is AT the VIN rail -- the DUT's documented
* enable interface (design/README.md "Enable/shutdown": active-high,
* full-rail 0V/VIN). Through record 20260926-043132-eba96ae VIN was pinned
* at 3.63V while EN kept 'vsup', which put EN 0.66V below VIN at the
* '*_2.97v' corners and stopped the block coming up at fs/125C.
* There is no operating-point solve in the
* deck at all -- the contract's `uic` + EN-edge shape, the one PR #170
* landed for sim/mc-output-accuracy and PR for #172 landed for
* line-/load-regulation. `td=6m` keeps the `fall=1` search off the
* start-up ramp's own rise, so the crossing found is the dropout event.
tran 10u 14m uic
meas tran dropout_vin_x find v(vin) when v(vout)=1.764 fall=1 td=6m
meas tran vout_at_max_vin_v avg v(vout) from=5.5m to=6m

measurements.name: dropout_v
measurements.note: Vin - Vout margin at the VIN where VOUT, as VIN is walked downward from 3.63V toward 1.5V, first falls through 1.764V (98% of the 1.8V ratified output target, i.e. the -2% departure-from-regulation point -- classic dropout-voltage definition) with I_LOAD at 50mA. Since #178 the downward walk is a quasi-static ramp (the shipped 8ms walk, 'vsup' -> 'vsup'-2.13V over 6ms-14ms, a constant 266.3 V/s at every corner since #187 made the endpoint track 'vsup') inside one cold-start `uic` transient rather than a `dc` sweep on a 20mV grid, so `meas tran ... when v(vout)=1.764 fall=1 td=6m` interpolates between adjacent timepoints of a continuous ramp (the `td=6m` keeps the search off the start-up ramp's own rise through 1.764V); there is no grid to quantize to at all. Fixed by issue #71 -- superseding #18's original `v(vin)[0] - v(vout)[0]` at a fixed low-VIN endpoint (1.9V), which measured deep past dropout rather than at the loss-of-regulation point (see #71 for the closed-loop screening that motivated this and design/README.md's campaign section for the corrected number). At -40C/27C this measurement is reliable (confirmed against independent per-point `.op` checks -- see the testbench schematic header). At 125C (all five process corners, not just the ff/sf thermal-shutdown false-trip #69 tracks) the underlying DC-solution-multiplicity #71 investigated is severe enough to corrupt this measurement at some corners (solver convergence failures, not real dropout numbers) -- read 125C dropout_v/vout_at_max_vin_v with the same caution already applied to ff/sf's 125C numbers, not as real measurements. Root-caused by #81: a genuine circuit robustness gap (a second, stable, non-regulating equilibrium the loop's own dynamics settle into at 125C/50mA, confirmed via a settled UIC transient seeded exactly at the intended point, not fixable by solver-seeding hardening) -- see design/README.md's campaign section ("#71/#81 resolved") and the testbench schematic header; fix deferred to #79. CORRECTED BY #169 (2026-09-25): that second equilibrium does not exist -- every initial condition, #81's own included, regulates at 125C/50mA (sim/ic-screen-125c-v/-f/-b/-c/-h), and #81's reported values are the regulating state's EA_OUT/TS_SNS/TS_REF; the 125C caution stands, but on the Newton non-convergence half alone, a bench problem tracked by #138/#168 (design/README.md section "#169"). THAT IS THE CAUTION #178 SET OUT TO CLEAR: the Newton non-convergence half was the unseeded `dc` sweep's own initial-condition defect, and #178 removed the `dc` sweep entirely (see the claim above). Whether the 125C caution is discharged is a measured question, answered per-corner by the first post-#178 record -- read that record's own narrative and sim/README.md's "#178" section rather than this note for the verdict. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Dropout @ 50 mA" row, < 300mV (stretch goal < 200mV, not applied here). ISSUE #187: the supply convention this number is measured under changed -- VIN's ramp now starts at 'vsup' with EN at that same rail, instead of a 3.63V-for-every-corner VIN with EN at 'vsup' -- and the ramp's endpoint tracks 'vsup' ('vsup'-2.13V) so the RATE stays the constant 266.3 V/s every earlier record ran at. Held that way the number is unchanged, not merely close: fs_125c_2.97v's crossing VIN reads 2.19615V under both conventions, i.e. dropout_v = 0.432153V to six digits. The rate is held deliberately: the intermediate record 20260926-100003-0b63ae4 kept the fixed 1.5V endpoint, which makes the rate per-supply and shifts this measurement by up to 20.4mV across the supply axis at the cold/slow corners (ss/27C 0.379823V at 2.97V vs 0.400265V at 3.63V) -- real rate-dependence at those corners, in the direction #178's ramp-rate caveat documents, and not something a supply axis should be carrying.

measurements.name: vout_at_max_vin_v
measurements.note: Vout at the ramp's starting (highest) VIN, which since issue #187 is the corner's own 'vsup' -- 2.97V, 3.30V or 3.63V -- rather than a 3.63V pinned for every corner. Ample headroom in every case. A wide sanity-range check (not a tight spec bound) that regulation is at least in a sane operating range at the easiest point of the run. Issue #178 changed how it is read: it is the settled 5.5ms-6ms tail average of the cold-start transient's own pre-ramp hold at that VIN (the same settle window sim/ic-screen-125c-c uses), replacing the pre-#178 `v(vout)[0]` -- the first point of a `dc VVIN` sweep that no longer exists. Same quantity, same settle window, measured on a physically realizable state instead of an unconstrained Newton solve. WHAT THE SUPERSEDED RECORD'S OUTLIER MEANT (issue #187): in 20260926-043132-eba96ae this measurement read -7.4521V at fs_125c_2.97v -- the single corner of that record outside this 0.5-3.7V band -- and -14.0589V at the same corner of 20260923-123440-d71f4b3. That was not a solver artifact (both corners' logs carry zero solver diagnostics) and not a dropout result: it was the bench's own EN-below-VIN supply convention. With VIN pinned at 3.63V and EN driven at 'vsup', EN sat 0.66V below VIN at the '*_2.97v' corners, which is off the DUT's documented enable interface (design/README.md "Enable/shutdown": EN is active-high, full-rail 0V/VIN). At EN = VIN-0.66V the M_ENP/M_ENP2 shutdown clamps stop being off -- 1.377uA and 1.639uA against a 39pA/62pA leakage floor at EN = VIN -- while M_ENP2's injection lifts BIASP by 90.6mV and starves every BIASP-gated PMOS current source, dropping the error amplifier's tail current from 3.476uA to 1.003uA. The clamp current into EA_OUT then exceeds the whole tail current that must sink it, EA_OUT is pulled to VIN, M_PASS turns off, and the bench's ideal 50mA sink discharges VOUT below ground (there is no clamp diode in this bench, so the reading is just -I*t/C_OUT, i.e. its magnitude is a bench artifact with no circuit meaning). It is a STATIC limit, not a start-up branch: bring the loop up at EN = VIN and then drop EN to 2.97V at 1ms and VOUT collapses from 1.82019V to -6.99V. And it is graded, not binary -- the whole '*_125c_2.97v' column of the superseded record read low (tt 1.76943V, ss 1.78627V, sf 1.79211V, ff 1.71701V against ~1.798V at their 3.30V/3.63V siblings) with fs the one corner that fell off the edge, because 125C maximizes the clamps' subthreshold conduction while fs (slow PMOS) minimizes the intended currents that must overcome it. #187 fixed the convention, not the circuit: EN now tracks VIN as it already does in every other bench in sim/ (sim/enable-shutdown exercises the EN edges themselves at 'vsup' = VIN).
